variants.title: Model the relationship
variants.context: Data modeling identifies entities, their relationships, and the rules connecting them.
variants.prompt: Each link belongs to one user, and a user owns many links. Which relationship fits?
options: Store ownership only in the link’s temporary cache entry.
Store a user_id column on each link row.
Store one link_id on the user, overwritten for each new link.
variants.hint: Separate a stable identity from fields that may change.
variants.explanation: A reference from each link represents its single owner.
optionFeedback: Revisit the requirement in the scenario. A reference from each link represents its single owner.

variants.title: Count child records
variants.context: One-to-many means a parent can own several children. Count each child once.
variants.prompt: 120 users each own exactly 5 links. How many link records are needed?
variants.hint: Multiply parents by children per parent.

mistakes.feedback: That adds 120 and 5. Each of the 120 users owns 5 links, so multiply.
That counts one row per user. One-to-many stores one row per link, not per owner.

variants.title: Protect customer boundaries
variants.context: A tenant is a customer or organization sharing a service with others. A record’s owner must be enforced when reading or changing it.
variants.prompt: Two tenants both use local link ID 7. What must a lookup distinguish?
options: The caller’s region without their tenant identity.
The tenant together with the local link ID.
Only local link ID 7 without tenant scope.
variants.hint: Ownership must remain attached to both identity and operations.
variants.explanation: A local ID may be unique only within its tenant.
optionFeedback: Revisit the requirement in the scenario. A local ID may be unique only within its tenant.
A local ID may be unique only within its tenant.
Revisit the requirement in the scenario. A local ID may be unique only within its tenant.

variants.title: Protect customer boundaries
variants.context: A tenant is a customer or organization sharing a service with others. A record’s owner must be enforced when reading or changing it.
variants.prompt: A request supplies another tenant’s ID. Which check is needed before returning their data?
options: Verify the signed-in caller is authorized for that tenant.
Trust the supplied ID because it is numeric.
Return every tenant’s rows and let the browser filter to one.
variants.hint: Ownership must remain attached to both identity and operations.
variants.explanation: User-supplied identifiers do not establish authorization.
optionFeedback: User-supplied identifiers do not establish authorization.
That choice does not preserve the stated requirement. User-supplied identifiers do not establish authorization.
Filtering in the browser still ships every tenant’s data to the client. User-supplied identifiers do not establish authorization.

variants.title: Protect customer boundaries

variants.prompt: Jobs from two customers are batched. What invariant should the batcher preserve?
options: Group only by job type, combining tenants in every batch.
Keep each batch scoped to its tenant.
Replace all tenant IDs with the first job’s tenant.
variants.hint: Ownership must remain attached to both identity and operations.
variants.explanation: Keeping the tenant boundary avoids mixing customer work.
